title: test_inspector.py finishes inside the verdict's 600 s bound, and a kill is told apart from slowness
intention: bin/cairn test cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py exits 0 well inside the verdict door's 600 s bound on the Dell, with every tooth printed, on three consecutive runs; its per-tooth durations are printed so a slow tooth is named, and the slow teeth move to sibling proof files rather than the bound being raised.
why: The verdict for the ticket whose id begins 9cfc was refused 'TIMEOUT, not disagreement': test_inspector.py ran 643.708 s and did not finish against the 600 s bound; an earlier re-run exited -9 (killed). Raising the bound moves the red, it does not remove it, and a -9 is a different cause (memory) from a slow run, so the cause must be measured before it is fixed. Trouble ticket-refused-9cfc.
traces_to: Law 3 (measure which: slow or killed), Law 8 (a verdict that cannot finish is no proof), Law 9.
how: Run the proof on the Dell under /usr/bin/time -v and print each tooth's wall time (the proof wraps each tooth in a timer); read dmesg/journal for an OOM kill on the -9 run. If slow: move the slowest teeth into sibling proof files so each file finishes under half the bound. If killed: find the tooth that holds the memory and bound it. The measurement is the first commit.

clauses.claim: bin/cairn test test_inspector.py finishes with exit 0 in under 300 s and prints every tooth, on three consecutive runs on the Dell
the proof prints each tooth's wall time, so a slow tooth is named in its own output

decisions.text: D1: time every tooth in test_inspector.py and print it with the PASS line; this is the measurement the fix is chosen from.
D2: the slowest teeth move to sibling proof files under the same proofs/ directory, one falsifier clause per tooth stays mapped by PROVES; the bound is not raised.

out: the verdict door and its 600 s bound

measured.saw: the 9cfc ticket's fixme n=1: VerdictRefused TIMEOUT, test_inspector.py ran 643.708 s and did not finish (bound 600 s); the earlier exit was -9 (orchestrator, 2026-11-14). Not yet known: which teeth take the time, or whether -9 was an OOM kill.
measured.how: read the fixme text in the 9cfc ticket's state file in CairnCommons/tickets and the orchestrator's cross-session message
